newsitem.title: ITALY: Iraq urges summit to end U.N. sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Iraq urges summit to end U.N. sanctions.

text.p: Iraq, complaining that U.N. sanctions had driven it into poverty, on Friday urged a summit on helping the world's hungry to end the punishment.
Aid agencies have said Iraq, crippled by sanctions imposed after it invaded Kuwait in 1990, faces a tough winter because food and medicines are in short supply.

Iraq's vice-president Taha Mohieddin Ma'rouf told the U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit in Rome that it should agree to "refrain from imposing economic embargos, the prevention of food and starving peoples in order to achieve political and economic aims".

Iraq says the United States is leading an attempt to crush the nation. Ma'rouf said sanctions "imposed in the name of the United Nations" had done nothing but spread famine, disease and poverty wherever they had been applied.

"They turn rich states into poor ones like what happened to my country, Iraq...The embargo imposed on Iraq has resulted in the destruction of the infrastructures of all the main sectors of production and services," he said.
The U.N. Security Council is the only body with the power to end sanctions but Ma'rouf made no reference to this.
Baghdad signed an agreement with the United Nations in May allowing it to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food and medicine.
The pact was about to be implemented in September but was halted when Baghdad sent in troops to northern Iraq to help one Kurdish faction fight another.
